Kuvitus: romuttamon nosturi. Nosturin pu: Illustration: a scrapyard crane. From the end of the boom of the crane a round grey electromagnet hangs on chains; it holds a rusty scrap car by its bottom and lifts it off a heap of scrap. In the background are heaps of scrap and the sky.
Schematic figure, not to scale, in two parts. On the left a vertical current-carrying wire through a table top seen from the side: a purple arrow shows the current upwards, and around the wire there are three green circular field lines whose arrows go round anticlockwise seen from above. On the right the same situation from above: the wire is a dot inside a circle, because the current comes towards the viewer, and around it there are three concentric field lines going anticlockwise. Four compasses on a field line: the north end of each needle, pink, points in the direction of the field line.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: pitkä käämi: Schematic figure, not to scale: a long coil cut along its length. The wire cross-sections in the upper row have a dot (current towards the viewer) and those in the lower row a cross (current away from the viewer). Inside the coil the green field lines are straight, evenly spaced and pointing to the right, so the field is almost uniform. Outside, the field lines curve from the right end back to the left. The right end is the north pole N and the left end the south pole S, as in a bar magnet.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: sähkömagnee: Schematic figure, not to scale: an electromagnet. A copper coil is wound round a vertical grey iron core, and the wires of the coil go to a battery and a switch. On the left the switch is closed and a current flows: the lower end of the iron core attracts iron nails, which hang from it in a chain. On the right the same electromagnet with the switch open: the blade of the switch is lifted off its contact, the circuit is broken and the nails have fallen onto the table.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: suoran johtimen m: Graph to scale: the magnetic flux density B of a straight wire in microtesla as a function of the distance r in centimetres, when the current is 10 A. The curve falls as the distance grows: at a distance of 1 cm B is 200 µT, at 2 cm it is 100 µT and at 4 cm it is 50 µT. When the distance doubles, the field is halved.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: käämi sivul: Schematic figure, not to scale: a coil seen from the side. The coil has N turns of copper wire over a length l. A current I, marked with a purple arrow, flows from the ends of the wire. Inside the coil a green arrow points along the axis; its label B is on the left of the coil, level with the arrow.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: käämin keskeltä m: Graph to scale: the magnetic flux density B measured at the centre of a coil, in millitesla, as a function of the current I in amperes. Six measured points at currents 0; 0.5; 1.0; 1.5; 2.0 and 2.5 A lie almost on a straight line, and a fitted line has been drawn through them. The grid spacing is 0.5 A and 1 mT.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: suoran johtimen m: Graph to scale: the magnetic flux density B of a straight wire in microtesla as a function of the distance r in centimetres. The curve falls as the distance grows. Three measured points are marked at the distances 1.0, 2.0 and 4.0 cm, with guide lines drawn from them to the axes. The grid spacing is 1 cm and 20 µT.
